rules: Edits that change only a window length, only the combining operator, or only the wrapper (RANK/CS_RANK/CS_ZSCORE) of an archive member lost 7 slots to the subtree gate this round (63 vs 189 on TS_MAX($high), + vs * on CS_RANK($earnings_per_share/$open)). Change the driving field, not the packaging.

The same packaging swaps do not decorrelate either: a retimed stochastic hit rho 0.966, $close/TS_MEAN($close,10) hit 0.819, and TS_RANK($volume,126) hit 0.801 against a dollar-volume z-score. Price-location, EMA-reversion, and volume-level slots are saturated; bring a different construct or skip that niche.

Multiplying a strong fundamental rank by a short-window price term just reproduces the fundamental: CS_ZSCORE($roa) * a 2-day high/open term hit rho 0.930 against plain RANK($roa), and the operating_margin*asset_turnover version hit 0.913. A price leg must carry real cross-sectional dispersion, not act as a near-constant multiplier.

Fundamental TS_DELTAs failed the cheap screen every time the partner was price or volume (|t| 0.77, 0.13, 0.00) and passed at 3.50 and 3.99 when the partner was a second fundamental rank. Keep TS_DELTA($fundamental, 63) in fundamental-only combinations.
Price-only geometry under 21 days has no edge on the cheap window: a 10-day (TS_MAX-TS_MIN)/TS_SUM scored |t| 0.56. Any price normalizer should span 21 days or more.

Fundamental-led proposals were accepted at 3.50 to 4.20; price_volume-only ones only reached 0.60 and 1.49. Spend most of the budget on fundamental pairings, and give the price leg the bounded-ratio shape of the 4.20 winner (TS_MEAN($high,21)/TS_MAX($high,21)).
A raw TS_STD($return,126) divisor dropped coverage to 0.883, while a 189-day window on $high survived. Cap $return windows near 63; put long windows on price levels instead.

Two rejections were free losses: $leverage_placeholder is not a field (it is $leverage), and RANK(TS_DELTA($roa,126)) was submitted twice in one round. Check the field list and the round's own proposal list before submitting.
